intervention.description: application of a highly efficient DFT-based method aided by a specially designed machine learning potential to substitute costly thermodynamic integration with free energy perturbation calculations

structure.description: ab initio phase-space distribution reproduced by machine learning potential

evidence_units.mechanism: the machine learning potential closely reproduces the ab initio phase-space distribution, allowing the costly thermodynamic integration to be fully substituted with more efficient free energy perturbation calculations
evidence_spans: Here, we propose a highly efficient DFT-based method aided by a specially designed machine learning potential.

As the machine learning potential can closely reproduce the ab initio phase-space distribution, even for multi-component alloys, the costly thermodynamic integration can be fully substituted with more efficient free energy perturbation calculations.
The method achieves overall savings of computational resources by 80% compared to current alternatives.

intervention.action: propose efficient ab initio based approach for liquid free energy calculations
intervention.description: Use a specially designed machine-learning interatomic potential (MTP) to generate snapshots and directly up-sample to the DFT level using free energy perturbation, skipping expensive ab initio MD simulations.

parameters.methodology: direct upsampling inspired by solid phase approach

evidence_units.mechanism: The phase-space distribution of the specially designed MTP closely overlaps with the ab initio distribution for the liquid, enabling direct up-sampling to the DFT level using a few snapshots from the MTP generated trajectories based on free energy perturbation.

outcome.property: free energy and thermodynamic properties of liquid and solid
outcome.measurement_method: ab initio free energy calculations using MTP and DFT

evidence_spans: Here, we propose an efficient ab initio based approach for liquid free energy calculations inspired by direct upsampling for solid phases.

As the phase-space distribution of the specially designed MTP closely overlaps with the ab initio distribution for the liquid, even for multi-component materials, it becomes possible to entirely skip the expensive ab initio MD simulations and directly up-sample to the DFT level using a few snapshots from the MTP generated trajectories based on free energy perturbation.

intervention.description: Combine thermodynamic properties of solid and liquid TaVCrW computed using the proposed direct upsampling approach.

evidence_units.mechanism: Combining the thermodynamic properties of solid and liquid allows determination of melting properties.
evidence_spans: The free energy and thermodynamic properties of solid TaVCrW are computed using the direct upsampling approach.

Combining the thermodynamic properties of solid and liquid TaVCrW, the melting properties of TaVCrW are obtained and compared to available CALPHAD data, including the heat capacity and bulk modulus of the liquid phase.

intervention.description: Use GGA-PBE and LDA exchange-correlation functionals to predict melting properties.

evidence_units.mechanism: Performance of different exchange-correlation functionals in predicting melting properties is evaluated.
evidence_spans: GGA-PBE and LDA exchange-correlation functionals are used, and their performance in predicting melting properties for the TaVCrW alloy is discussed.

intervention.action: replace thermodynamic integration with free energy perturbation
intervention.description: Utilizing a machine learning potential (MTP) with high accuracy to enable free energy perturbation (FEP) instead of thermodynamic integration (TI) for correcting the MTP free energy to DFT accuracy.

structure.description: Liquid phase with high overlap between MTP and DFT phase space distributions

evidence_units.mechanism: High accuracy of the MTP provides a strong overlap with the ab initio liquid phase space, enabling efficient free energy perturbation calculations with few uncorrelated snapshots.

outcome.property: Energy difference between MTP and DFT (liquid free energy correction)
outcome.measurement_method: Comparison of free energy perturbation and thermodynamic integration

evidence_spans: The number of required snapshots depends on the root-mean-square error (RMSE) of the MTP, following the relation (2RMSE/ c ) 2 , where ± c represents the target accuracy. This relationship has been tested and discussed in detail in ref. [19] . According to the RMSE of the MTP (here 2.6 meV/atom for GGA-PBE calculations), to attain an accuracy of 1 meV/atom, only approximately 28 uncorrelated snapshots are needed, as depicted in Fig. 2 a.
The energy differences between the MTP and DFT computed by free energy perturbation and thermodynamic integration are relatively small (0.5 meV/atom), as shown in Fig. 2 a, b.
limitations: MTP optimized solely for liquid phase DFT phase space; transferability to other parts of phase space not guaranteed.

intervention.action: calculate free energy surface using proposed EAM+MTP+FEP method
intervention.description: Computing the ab initio free energy surface on a 5 × 6 ( V , T ) grid using the optimized hierarchical approach replacing EAM with MTP and TI with FEP.

structure.description: Free energy surface of liquid TaVCrW

evidence_units.mechanism: Substitution of computationally expensive thermodynamic integration (TI) and classical EAM potentials with machine learning potential (MTP) and free energy perturbation (FEP) theory reduces computational effort while maintaining DFT accuracy.
evidence_spans: Table 1 CPU time in core hours needed by the original and hybrid TOR-TILD method and the newly proposed approach for computing the ab initio free energy surface of liquid TaCrVW on a 5 × 6 ( V , T ) grid using LDA
Compared to the original TOR-TILD method, the proposed approach is about 20 times faster in the total CPU time.
The overall acceleration is attributed to substituting EAM with MTP and TI with FEP.
limitations: None explicitly stated for this specific comparison unit.

material.name: TaVCrW
material.initial_state: solid and liquid phases at equilibrium

intervention.action: include electronic contribution to free energy
intervention.description: Calculating the electronic density of states (DOS) including electron-vibration coupling at elevated temperatures.

structure.description: Solid and liquid phases with electronic excitations and electron-vibration coupling

evidence_units.mechanism: Electronic contribution to free energy differs between solid and liquid phases due to a gap in the DOS at the Fermi level, resulting in a difference in electronic Gibbs energy.

outcome.property: Melting point shift due to electronic contribution
outcome.measurement_method: Comparison with calculations without electronic contribution

evidence_spans: Correspondingly, this gap translates to an electronic Gibbs energy difference of 4.2 meV/atom between the solid and liquid, leading to a shift in the melting point by 48 K compared to calculations that do not account for the electronic contribution.
limitations: None explicitly stated for this specific comparison unit.

intervention.action: account for short-range order (SRO) using on-lattice machine learning potentials
intervention.description: Performing Monte Carlo simulations to compute configurational internal energy, entropy, and free energy differences relative to ideal random alloy.

evidence_units.mechanism: SRO decreases internal energy but also slightly reduces configurational entropy; the net effect is a stabilization of the solid free energy.

outcome.property: Solid free energy stabilization due to SRO

evidence_spans: However, SRO also decreases the internal energy by about 8–9 meV/atom (Fig. 4 d). Hence the resulting free energy of the solid is overall stabilized by about 2.4 meV/atom, Fig. 4 a, resulting in a slight shift of the melting temperature as discussed further below.
limitations: Assumes ideal mixing for the baseline; SRO quantified via low-rank potentials.

intervention.description: applied hierarchical approach integrating EAM, MTP, and DFT with free energy perturbation

structure.description: liquid and solid phases of bcc TaVCrW

evidence_units.mechanism: free energy perturbation calculations replace expensive thermodynamic integration, leveraging MTP advantages to reduce computational effort while retaining accuracy
evidence_spans: The approach has been applied to the bcc refractory high entropy alloy TaVCrW, for which currently no experimental data of melting properties exist.
Both our DFT predictions are below the CALPHAD extracted value (2569 K) by 193 K for GGA-PBE and 160 K for LDA.
limitations: CALPHAD input data includes only sub-binary alloy information
High-temperature magnetic fluctuations not included for Cr and V
SRO contribution estimated to be small (~25 K shift)

intervention.description: included electronic excitations and their coupling to lattice vibrations in the DFT calculation

evidence_units.mechanism: electronic excitations couple to lattice vibrations, shifting the melting temperature

outcome.property: melting point shift due to electronic excitations

evidence_spans: In the present work, given that tungsten constitutes 1/4 of the investigated TaVCrW alloy, the induced change in melting point is smaller but still significant (48 K for GGA-PBE and 57 K for LDA) and again highlights the necessity to include the electronic contribution into melting point considerations.

intervention.description: applied hierarchical approach with LDA functional

evidence_units.mechanism: overbinding property of LDA functional increases predicted melting point relative to GGA-PBE

outcome.property: melting temperature shift relative to CALPHAD

evidence_spans: Both our DFT predictions are below the CALPHAD extracted value (2569 K) by 193 K for GGA-PBE and 160 K for LDA.

intervention.description: tested impact of magnetic fluctuations using GGA-PBE based on high-temperature MD snapshots

evidence_units.mechanism: spin-polarized calculations reveal negligible impact of magnetic fluctuations on melting properties
evidence_spans: We have performed additional spin-polarized test calculations using GGA-PBE based on high-temperature MD snapshots, revealing a negligible impact.
